# Law coverage book

<!-- Generated by `npm run legal:coverage-book` from packages/legal-rules/catalogue/section-review and the shipped packs. Do not edit by hand. -->

What the block planner's legal rules reach in each statute, regulation and Omineca order PGMaps stores, section by section. Read on 2026-11-27. This is a machine-assisted reading, not a legal review: whether a rule or a map screen cites a section is a fact about the packs, and what each section bears on and what is left is a reading of its text. The contract is [Block planning and Prince George forest patch scenarios](forestry-patch-scenarios.md), **The law behind a finding**; what to build next is in [Block planner: next steps](forestry-block-planning-next-steps.md).

**How to read a row.**

- *A rule cites it*: a pack rule cites the section, so a block review asks about it. The note says what the rule still leaves to the reviewer.
- *A map screen cites it*: only a map screen of *On this ground* cites it.
- *Gap: high*, *medium* or *low*: no rule cites it and the reading found something a block review should test, by priority.
- *Not about a block*: administration, tenure, enforcement, definitions or repealed text. These are listed by number only.

| medium | Integrated Pest Management Act, SBC 2003 c. 58 | s. 7 | Herbicide brushing on Omineca blocks is done under a licensee's or BC Timber Sales' pest management plan; no rule checks that the block lies within a plan area with a confirmed pesticide use notice, or that confirmation is not approval of the plan. |
| medium | Prince George TSA Landscape Biodiversity Objectives Implementation Policy, revised December 2005 | Policy 4 ¶2 | No rule flags a block or merged opening over 500 ha that lacks retention patches over 10 ha. Policy, not binding, but it is a per-opening test the planner could make from drawn retention. |
| medium | District Managers' Letter of Expectations for implementing the Prince George TSA biodiversity order, 21 December 2022 | Methodology ¶2 | The ministry counts only the old forest inside these areas and includes UWRs, WHAs and WTRAs; the code counts legal and non-legal OGMAs whole (as order D.1's "entire area" says), parks by switch, and UWR, WHA and WTRA old forest only as ordinary old forest. The planner's surplus or deficit will differ from Appendix 2's net targets; the record should say which accounting it used. |
| medium | 2006 Omineca Agriculture Development Areas and Settlement Reserve Areas Order | Part I | The ground screen reads the extent polygons from DataBC; every rule takes "does the order apply" as the reviewer's answer. The maps are marked DRAFT and not for legal purposes, so the screen can only suggest; a rule could pre-fill the applicability question from the screen as a candidate. |
| medium | Amendment Order for the Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 23 September 2010 | 1(a) | The planner holds no Mackenzie old forest unit, table or rule: the old forest module covers only the PG TSA order (orderUnits.ts refuses Mackenzie). Only the generic legal-objective screen could show the order if DataBC maps its extent. The January 2010 map is not attached to the copy reviewed. |
| medium | Ministerial Order: Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 9 April 2008 | 1.2 | Not modelled. The 600 ha qualifier is ambiguous: it can be read to limit only community forests or all three tenures; a reviewer must decide. Note also it names research forests, which the PG TSA order does not. |
| medium | Ministerial Order: Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 9 April 2008 | Map #1 | Landscape unit polygons are on DataBC (RMP_LANDSCAPE_UNIT_SVW) and could be read as the PG units are. |
| medium | Ministerial Order: Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 9 April 2008 | Objective 2(a) | Unlike the PG TSA, the cap is in the order itself. Needs the affected share of the unit and the NFA share of what is counted. |
| medium | Ministerial Order: Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 9 April 2008 | Objective 2(c) | Not modelled; a rule like PG D.5(a) would ask whether a deficit exists and whether recruitment stands are identified. |
| medium | Ministerial Order: Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 9 April 2008 | Objective 3(a) | As 2(c), for interior. |
| medium | Ministerial Order: Non-spatial Landscape Biodiversity Objectives in the Mackenzie Forest District, 9 April 2008 | Guidance 4 | Same as the PG 2005 method except lakes are also buffered; the PG interior code could be reused with lakes added. |
| medium | Order to Establish a Sensitive Area and Objectives, Mugaha Marsh, 2001 | Objective 1 | The legal-objective screen shows the area with harvest reach unknown; a rule could flag overlap and ask the objective's question, citing the plan's strategies as guidance. |
| medium | Order to Establish the Obo River and Fox Landscape Units and Objectives, 2002 | 1.A.a | The patch analysis runs the PG TSA Table 7 classes only; Obo-Fox Table 1 has its own classes (up to 1000 ha) split by NDT, and the unit boundaries are not in any layer the planner reads. |
| medium | Order to Establish the Obo River and Fox Landscape Units and Objectives, 2002 | 1.A.e | No rule records a deviation approval beside a Table 1 result. |
| medium | Order to Establish the Obo River and Fox Landscape Units and Objectives, 2002 | 1.A.f | The old forest module calculates the PG TSA order only. The 2008 Mackenzie non-spatial order says it applies where it conflicts on old (it names 1.A.g and Table 2), so a rule would test mature-plus-old here and old under the 2008 order. |
| medium | Order establishing Scenic Areas in the Prince George Forest District, 2005 | 1(a) | The inventory screens draw the scenic polygons; the designation adds nothing a rule can test without the VQO, so the gap sits with the VQO order. |

### Forest Planning and Practices Regulation, BC Reg 14/2004

`bc.fppr` · [BC Laws](https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/14_2004) · read 2026-11-27

| Section | Status | Bears on | Cited by | What is left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| s. 1 | A rule cites it | Defines the terms the practice rules turn on, including net area to be reforested (1(2)), standards unit, soil disturbance, permanent access structure, stream and fish stream, wildlife tree retention area and minor tenure. | `bc.crown-grazing@1.0.0:nar-reserved`, `bc.crown-grazing@1.1.0:nar-reserved`, `ground:uwr-no-harvest`, `ground:uwr-conditional`, `ground:uwr-uncoded`, `ground:wha-no-harvest`, `ground:wha-conditional`, `ground:wha-uncoded`, `ground:community-watershed`, `ground:water-licence`, `ground:recreation-site`, `ground:recreation-trail`, `ground:visual-quality-objective`, `ground:scenic-area` | The net area to be reforested is entered as a verified figure rather than derived from the block's geometry by subtracting the six 1(2) exclusions (permanent access, non-productive and non-commercial patches of at least 0.1 ha and 10 m wide, wildlife tree retention areas, riparian reserve zones, reserved areas); only exclusion (f) has its own rule. The 'stream' and 'fish stream' definitions (20% gradient presumption, 100 m channel) drive every riparian class but are not asked. |
| s. 1.1 | A rule cites it | Sets the five categories (preservation to maximum modification) by which an altered forest landscape seen from a significant public viewpoint is judged against a visual quality objective. | `bc.omineca.visual-quality@1.0.0:over-preservation`, `bc.omineca.visual-quality@1.0.0:over-retention`, `bc.omineca.visual-quality@1.0.0:over-partial-retention`, `bc.omineca.visual-quality@1.0.0:over-modification`, `bc.omineca.visual-quality@1.0.0:over-maximum-modification`, `ground:visual-quality-objective`, `ground:scenic-area` | Rules now name the order and test the alteration entered from the visual quality page against the category; the planner does not read that page’s measurement itself. |
| s. 2 | Gap: low | Makes every riparian and Division 4 watershed distance a slope distance, and exempts a person from Part 4 and 5 practice requirements as needed to conform to the Workers Compensation Act. |  | The riparian width rules compare an entered width with the table minimum without saying the statutory distance is slope distance; a width taken off a map is horizontal and should be stated as such (it is conservative, never short, against the slope-distance minimum). |
| s. 4.03 | Gap: low | Requires a forest operations plan to contain all the information Division 2 lists. |  | No FOP content check exists; the planner does not hold FOP documents. |
| s. 4.04 | Gap: low | Requires the FOP to carry each holder's current business contact information. |  | Paperwork only; not a block test. |
| s. 4.05 | Gap: low | Requires a unique identifier and amendment count on the FOP. |  | Paperwork only. |
| s. 4.06 | Gap: low | Requires the FOP to state its submission and approval dates. |  | Paperwork only; the approval date could anchor a check that the block was in an approved plan before harvest. |
| s. 4.07 | Gap: low | Requires the approved FOP to state its term and expiry date. |  | A rule could compare a scheduled harvest year with the FOP's expiry, but the planner records no FOP term. |
| s. 4.08 | Gap: low | Requires an extended FOP to record the extension date and new expiry. |  | Paperwork only. |
| s. 4.09 | Gap: low | Requires the FOP to name the forest districts and regions it covers. |  | Paperwork only. |
| s. 4.11 | Gap: medium | Requires the FOP to list every existing and proposed cutblock and road, each proposed one with a unique identifier. |  | Under the FOP regime a block can be harvested only if it is listed in the plan; nothing asks whether the planned block appears in an approved FOP under its identifier. |
| s. 4.12 | Gap: medium | Requires the FOP to state the year harvesting of each proposed cutblock, and construction of each proposed road, is to begin. |  | The planner's schedule holds a harvest year per block; nothing compares it with the commencement year stated in the FOP. |
| s. 4.13 | Gap: low | Requires any assessment a planning guideline calls for to be submitted with the FOP or amendment. |  | Paperwork only. |

A block in any of them also cannot be added by a no-approval amendment (s. 4.43(1)(a)(i)). |

### Government Actions Regulation, BC Reg 582/2004

`bc.gar` · [BC Laws](https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/582_2004) · read 2026-11-27

| Section | Status | Bears on | Cited by | What is left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| s. 2 | Gap: medium | Requires a minister making a GAR order to be satisfied it is consistent with established objectives and that public benefit outweighs impacts on delivered wood costs and tenure rights; and says an order does not apply to cutting permits, road permits, TSLs without CPs, BCTS forestry licences to cut and (unless stated) minor tenures entered into before it takes effect, to declared areas, or to FRPA s. 196(1) and FPPR s. 110 areas. |  | The UWR, WHA and other GAR-order screens show the designation without asking whether the block's cutting permit, road permit or TSL predates the order, which (2)(a) says takes it outside the order. The crown-grazing pack asks the parallel question for the ADA/SRA order. |
| s. 5 | Gap: medium | Lets the Forest Act minister identify resource features by order (karst, range developments, research land, snow courses, unregulated cultural heritage resources of traditional use, authorized recreation trails and facilities, significant recreation features), with undisclosed locations notified only to affected holders under confidentiality conditions. |  | Recreation sites and trails are screened and range developments are handled by the crown-grazing range-development rule under FRPA s. 51, but karst, research installations, snow courses and cultural heritage resource features have no screen, and confidential features can only be asked about. |
| s. 6 | Gap: low | Lets the Forest Act minister establish a lakeshore management zone of a stated width beside an L1 lake, with objectives, where forest resources need special management. |  | No screen reads lakeshore management zones; they apply to L1 lakes where no default riparian zone exists. |
| s. 7 | A rule cites it | Lets the Land Act minister establish scenic areas, and the Forest Act minister set visual quality objectives for them within the FPPR s. 1.1 categories. | `bc.omineca.visual-quality@1.0.0:vqo-established`, `ground:visual-quality-objective`, `ground:scenic-area` | Rules now name the order and test the alteration entered from the visual quality page against the category; the planner does not read that page’s measurement itself. |
| s. 8 | Gap: medium | Lets the Land Act minister designate the drainage upslope of a domestic licensed waterworks intake as a community watershed, and the Wildlife Act minister set water quality objectives for it. | `ground:community-watershed` | The community watershed screen cites this section; no rule reads the watershed's water quality objectives and asks whether the block meets them. |
| s. 9 | Gap: medium | Lets the Wildlife Act minister establish general wildlife measures for a category of species at risk, regionally important wildlife or ungulates over a specified area, or for a wildlife habitat area or ungulate winter range. | `ground:uwr-no-harvest`, `ground:uwr-conditional`, `ground:uwr-uncoded`, `ground:wha-no-harvest`, `ground:wha-conditional`, `ground:wha-uncoded` | Measures attached to a UWR or WHA (subsection (2)) feed the screens' reach cells; species-category measures over a specified area under subsection (1) are not read at all. |
| s. 9.1 | Gap: low | Lets the Wildlife Act minister establish general measures for categories of ecological communities at risk over a specified area. |  | No screen reads ecological community measures; few exist. |

| s. 11 | Gap: medium | Lets the Wildlife Act minister identify wildlife habitat features (fisheries and marine sensitive features, significant mineral licks or wallows, nests of bald eagles, ospreys, great blue herons or listed birds, other localized features), with sensitive locations withheld. |  | No screen reads wildlife habitat features and no rule asks about them, though FPPR s. 70(2) bars damaging them. |
| s. 12 | Gap: medium | Lets the Wildlife Act minister establish ungulate winter ranges and their objectives where winter habitat for specified ungulates needs special management. | `ground:uwr-no-harvest`, `ground:uwr-conditional`, `ground:uwr-uncoded` | The UWR screens read the ranges and apply their general wildlife measures to reach cells; no rule reads a UWR objective's terms (for example retention or forage targets) against the block. |
| s. 14 | Gap: low | Lets the Wildlife Act minister identify fisheries sensitive watersheds (significant downstream fisheries values and watershed sensitivity) and set objectives for them. |  | No screen reads FSW orders; check whether any exist in the Omineca before building one. |
| s. 15 | Gap: low | Lets the Wildlife Act minister designate part of a fish stream as a temperature sensitive stream where streamside trees are needed to manage its temperature. |  | No screen reads TSS designations; FPPR s. 53 depends on them. |
| s. 16 | Gap: low | Continues as GAR community watersheds those established under the Code after 31 January 2004 and existing when this section took effect. |  | The community watershed screen reads all designated watersheds; the route by which one was established matters only for which objective applies (FPPR s. 8.2). |
| s. 17 | A map screen cites it | Continues as a visual quality objective a visual quality class set before 24 October 2002 by district manager letter or in an approved TFL visual landscape inventory. | `ground:visual-quality-objective` | The VQO screen reads the published layer; a class continued only by a district manager's letter may not appear there, so a reviewer may need to ask. |
| s. 18 | Gap: low | Applies the FPPR s. 1.1 categories of altered forest landscape to continued visual quality objectives. |  | Same gap as FPPR s. 1.1: no rule tests a block against the category. |
| s. 19 | Gap: low | Continues Code-era resource features (from higher level plans or made known to licence and woodlot holders) as GAR s. 5 resource features. |  | Continued features known only from old notices to the holder can only be asked about. |
